title: Special Workers: Apprentices, Learners, and PWDs
description: Book II training and employment of special workers in syllabus order: apprentices (Arts. 58-61, 72), learners (Arts. 73-76), and persons with disabilities (Arts. 78-81, RA 7277) — with the apprentice-vs-learner table and the 75% wage-floor cross-links to the wages lesson.

blocks.markdown: Special workers — objectives: qualify apprentices and learners, enforce agreement contents and wage floors, apply the learner conversion rule, and employ PWDs under Arts. 78-81 and RA 7277.

Book II creates **three lawful training/employment tracks** that temper general labor standards: **apprentices** (long technical training + theory), **learners** (short semi-skilled training), and **PWD workers** (impaired earning capacity). The design logic is identical across all three: **open opportunities without cheapening labor** — written agreements, wage floors (the uniform **75%**), time caps, and anti-undercutting gates. Every 75% floor here cross-links to the wages lesson (Art. 124 auto-modifies training wage clauses on each increase), and terminology has modernized: the Code's 'handicapped workers' are today's **persons with disabilities (PWDs)** under RA 7277.
Apprentices (Arts. 58-61, 72)

Four interlocking definitions: **apprenticeship = OJT + theory**; apprentice status needs a **written agreement**; apprenticeable = **>3 months** training; and the agreement is itself an **employment contract**.
Three qualifications: **age 14+, vocational aptitude, ability to follow instructions** — with the currency note that RA 9231 now sets the operative child-labor floor at 15.
The double gate: **highly-technical-industry employers only**, in **Secretary-approved occupations only**. Outside these gates the 'apprentice' label collapses into regular employment analysis.

Three controls: Secretary-conforming agreement, **period <= 6 months**, and sub-minimum wages **only in approved programs, never below 75%** of the applicable minimum. The syllabus's '61' under minimum wage.
The **only** unpaid apprenticeship: **school/curriculum-required OJT individually authorized by the Secretary**. Both conditions, every time — employer say-so never suffices.

**Compliance checklist** for apprentice hiring: (1) confirm highly-technical industry + approved occupation (Art. 60); (2) execute the **written** agreement conforming to Secretary rules (Arts. 58(d), 61); (3) cap the period at **6 months** and calendar expiry (work beyond converts toward regular status); (4) pay **>=75% of the CURRENT minimum** (re-verify after each wage order; Art. 124 auto-modifies the clause); (5) for unpaid OJT, secure **both** the school requirement and the Secretary authorization (Art. 72). **Exam move**: any 'apprentice' fact pattern missing the writing, the gates, or the program fails into regular-employment analysis.
Learners (Arts. 73-76)
The learner in one sentence: trainee in a **semi-skilled, non-apprenticeable** occupation, OJT-learnable in **<=3 months**. The 3-month ceiling is the bright line against apprentices.

Three cumulative justifications: **no experienced workers available + necessary to prevent curtailment + no labor-cost undercutting or standards impairment**. The anti-abuse gate against rotating 'learners' to save 25%.

Four mandatory contents — names, **<=3-month duration**, **>=75% wage**, and the **commitment to hire as regulars** — plus the sting: **2-month work + early no-fault termination = automatic regular status**.
One line with bite: **piece-rate learners are paid in full** — no 75% training discount. Time-learners 75%, piece-learners 100%.

blocks.markdown: Persons with disabilities (Arts. 78-81, RA 7277)
The gateway: **earning capacity impaired** by age, physical/mental deficiency, or injury. 'Handicapped workers' in the Code = **PWDs** in current usage (and in the syllabus).
The PWD twin of Art. 74: **necessity + no-undercutting** — with NO unavailability requirement. PWD hiring is encouraged even where experienced workers exist.
Four contents mirroring learnership — names, **>=75% rate**, duration, work to be performed — in a **DOLE-inspectable** agreement. The syllabus's '80 par. 2' under minimum wage.

The bridge: PWDs may train as **apprentices or learners** whenever the handicap does not effectively impede the **particular** occupation's operations. Art. 81 routes trainees; Arts. 78-80 govern workers.

The modern rule alongside Arts. 78-81: **no denial of suitable employment**, and qualified PWD employees get **identical terms, compensation, and benefits** as able-bodied counterparts. Later amendments touched only privileges.

Resolve the apparent 75%-vs-equality tension by scope: **Art. 80's 75%** governs the covered employment-agreement period (the training-rate permission); **RA 7277 Sec. 5** governs qualified PWD employees generally (equal pay for equal work — the same 'work of equal value' logic as Art. 133(a)). **Routing drill**: PWD hired to train -> test Art. 81 (does the handicap impede THIS occupation?) -> apprentice track (Arts. 58-72) or learner track (Arts. 73-76) as the occupation fits; PWD hired to work -> Art. 79 gate + Art. 80 agreement. RA 7277 adds a 5% casual/emergency/contractual-post reserve in listed social-development agencies (Sec. 6) and confirms apprenticeship eligibility (Sec. 7). **Remember**: 'handicapped' is Code vocabulary; answer in PWD terms and cite both regimes.

blocks.markdown: **Top traps for this topic**: (1) calling any trainee an 'apprentice' outside highly-technical industries/approved occupations; (2) exceeding the 6-month apprentice or 3-month learner caps; (3) paying piece-learners 75% (Art. 76: full pay); (4) terminating a learnership before month 3 without learner fault (Art. 75: auto-regular); (5) unpaid OJT without BOTH school requirement and Secretary authorization; (6) applying Art. 80's 75% as a permanent PWD discount (RA 7277 Sec. 5: qualified PWDs get equality).
Can I recite the apprentice-vs-learner table from memory (occupation, period, floor, gate, post-training rule) and route a PWD trainee vs PWD worker correctly?
Can I state every 75% floor with its article and condition, the Art. 72 unpaid exception, and the Art. 75 auto-regularization tripwire?

**Takeaways**: (1) Three tracks, one logic — **open opportunities, never cheapen labor**: writing + floors + caps + gates. (2) **Apprentice = >3 months + theory + 6-month cap**; **learner = semi-skilled + 3-month cap + hire commitment**; piece-learners always full pay. (3) The **75% is uniform but conditional** — approved programs, current minimums, auto-modification — and RA 7277 Sec. 5 overlays **equality for qualified PWDs**. (4) The two tripwires: **Art. 72** (unpaid needs school + Secretary) and **Art. 75** (early no-fault cut = regular). This closes the labor module: hours set the time, wages price it, leaves excuse absence from it, and special-workers rules temper all three during training.
